subjects.description: Small orange rectangular block attached to the bottom of a vertical coil spring

observation.what_happens: An orange block attached to a vertical spring oscillates up and down in the center of the frame. The motion starts from a low stretched position and continues as free vertical oscillation, ending still in motion.

calibration.note: no scale: lengths are in pixels

reasoning: The track is a straight vertical line with large back-and-forth motion in s whose envelope shrinks from ~250 pix to ~80 pix over 4.5 s, so it is a decaying free spring oscillation in air. Candidates go from textbook undamped to linear viscous damping to linear plus quadratic air drag to test what energy loss predicts the hidden future best.

critique.finding: The block bounces like a damped spring that stiffens as it stretches, hanging around {s_eq} and losing energy with {gamma}. It only partly captures the motion and leaves a big regular wobble.
critique.headline: Spring block bounces on with stiffness that grows as it stretches.
critique.revision_idea: Add dry Coulomb friction that takes a fixed bite each swing. The misses swing regularly above and below zero with shifting bin means, showing amplitude falls differently than viscous damping alone allows.
critique.why_it_won: It gets the changing pace of big stretches right while plain linear springs keep ringing at the wrong pace.

preRevision.revision_idea: Add a cubic hardening stiffness to the spring pull. The misses swing positive and negative with the bob, showing the tone shifts with stretch, which a linear pull cannot follow.

postRevision.revision_idea: Add dry Coulomb friction that takes a fixed bite each swing. The misses swing regularly above and below zero with shifting bin means, showing amplitude falls differently than viscous damping alone allows.

headline: Spring block bounces on with stiffness that grows as it stretches.
finding: The block bounces like a damped spring that stiffens as it stretches, hanging around about 100 px and losing energy with about 0.48 1/s. It only partly captures the motion and leaves a big regular wobble.

eyeball.confidence: low - visual count of ~6-7 cycles in ~7 s gives w0 ~8-9 rad/s; envelope decays over several seconds giving gamma ~0.5-1.0 1/s; equilibrium mid-point between extremes roughly estimated in image pixels from top
eyeball.law_in_words: vertical position s(t) follows damped harmonic oscillator about equilibrium: d2s/dt2 = -w0^2*(s - s_eq) - gamma*ds/dt, with s measured downward in pixels from top of image

truth.note: This clip was rendered from a law drawn by public randomness (drand round 6604981) and sealed before the run: its SHA-256 was committed and pushed in 4b94c8b, the law revealed in 9997e76. Missed. The drawn law was a cubic hardening spring with dry (Coulomb) friction and a periodic drive; Muse Wonder found the cubic hardening but kept viscous damping, and no model proposed the drive. The second referee then asked for dry friction, the right term, but no second revision runs. With no ruler found, lengths are in pixels; true values in pixels use the render's own scale.

si.scale: the render's own scale, 0.00127 m per pixel (orthographic camera)

drawn.equation: x'' = -(k/m) x - (k3/m) x^3 - mu sign(x') + F0 cos(wd t)
drawn.x: displacement below the resting point (m, down positive); t from release

mu.rule: the swing dies in N half cycles, N uniform in [10, 16] (drawn 15.39); mu = w0^2 A / (2N)

F0.rule: F0 / |w0^2 - wd^2| = share of A uniform in [0.15, 0.35] (drawn 0.191)

wd.rule: wd / w0 uniform in [0.55, 0.8] or [1.25, 1.6], each half the time (drawn 1.587)
